name: Granite Speech 4.1 2B NAR
purpose: Latency-sensitive ASR: edits a CTC hypothesis in a single forward pass instead of decoding token by token (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card metadata: apache-2.0; the repo has no LICENSE file. Canonical Apache-2.0 text read in the Qwen repo (canonical Apache-2.0 text read in https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-ASR/blob/main/LICENSE).

architecture.kind: NON-AUTOREGRESSIVE (NLE): 440M CTC Conformer + 160M Q-Former + 1B bidirectional LLM editor (granite-4.0-1b-base + LoRA)
architecture.why_this_design: Single-pass CTC-hypothesis editing for latency-sensitive applications (card).

benchmarks.name: German WER, Open ASR multilingual track (4 of 8 datasets)
benchmarks.harness: Open ASR Leaderboard multilingual track, German column (WER %), read from the Space config JSON 2026-11-19; rows differ in how many of the 8 datasets they cover

benchmarks.name: Open ASR English avg WER (leaderboard rank 43 of 69)
benchmarks.harness: Open ASR Leaderboard English track, read 2026-11-19

benchmarks.name: RTFx on the leaderboard (English track, leaderboard GPU)
MLS German WER / CommonVoice 15 German WER

weaknesses: Less accurate than the autoregressive 4.1-2b; no punctuation

tona_fit.reason: Quality is solid but not best (German 4.32 on 4 of 8 sets, English 7.16) and RTFx is very high (2112); it needs flash-attn 2, a risk on gfx1200. The former reject was only about missing Tona support; now a speed-niche option next to the Parakeet class.
